def-nrqmx-smooth-projector-bundle:
## Definition

Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional smooth manifold, let $d\geq1$ be an integer, and give $\mathbb C^d$ its standard Hermitian inner product. Let $P:M\to\operatorname{End}(\mathbb C^d)$ be a $C^2$ map such that $P(x)^2=P(x)=P(x)^*$ and $\operatorname{rank}P(x)=r$ is constant. Define
$$E_P=\{(x,v)\in M\times\mathbb C^d:P(x)v=v\},\qquad \pi(x,v)=x.$$
Its fiber at $x$ is $\operatorname{ran}P(x)$ with the inner product inherited from $\mathbb C^d$. For a $C^1$ section $s:U\to\mathbb C^d$ over an open $U\subseteq M$ satisfying $P s=s$, define the projected connection by $\nabla s=P\,ds$, where $d$ is the componentwise exterior derivative. For a $C^2$ path $\gamma:[0,1]\to M$, put $P_\gamma(t)=P(\gamma(t))$ and $K_\gamma(t)=[P_\gamma'(t),P_\gamma(t)]$. Kato transport along $\gamma$ is the matrix solution $W_\gamma'(t)=K_\gamma(t)W_\gamma(t)$, $W_\gamma(0)=I_d$.

The connection and Kato transport are defined from the projector family itself; no Schrödinger Hamiltonian or physical time evolution is needed. A coherent uniformly gapped spectral projection of a $C^2$ finite Hermitian family is one source of such a $C^2$ family: under Countable Choice, an earlier finite-dimensional adiabatic result supplies that regularity.
lem-nrqmx-projector-bundle-kato-well-def:
## Statement

Let $M$, $d$, and $P$ satisfy [[def-nrqmx-smooth-projector-bundle]], and write $E_P$ for its range family. Then $E_P\to M$ is a rank-$r$ $C^2$ complex vector bundle, and $\nabla s=P\,ds$ is a Hermitian connection on it. For every $C^2$ path $\gamma:[0,1]\to M$, the Kato equation $W'=[P_\gamma',P_\gamma]W$, $W(0)=I_d$, has a unique $C^2$ solution. That solution is unitary and satisfies $P_\gamma(t)W(t)=W(t)P_\gamma(0)$ for every $t\in[0,1]$.
lem-nrqmx-c1-stokes-compact-surface:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $M$ be a compact oriented smooth surface with boundary, and let $D\subseteq M$ be a compact oriented region whose boundary consists of finitely many $C^2$ arcs meeting at finitely many corners. Let $\eta=a\,dx+b\,dy$ be a complex-valued $C^1$ one-form on a neighborhood of $D$ in each local chart, where $C^1$ means its coefficients and first partial derivatives are continuous up to the boundary. Define $d\eta=(\partial_xb-\partial_ya)\,dx\wedge dy$ in each chart; the chain rule and symmetry of second derivatives make this expression coordinate-independent. Give $\partial D$ the outward-normal-first orientation. Then
$$\int_D d\eta=\int_{\partial D}\eta.$$
thm-nrqmx-berry-projector-curvature:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $M$, $d$, and $P$ satisfy [[def-nrqmx-smooth-projector-bundle]], with constant rank $r$. The curvature of the projected connection $\nabla=P\,d$, as an endomorphism-valued two-form on $\mathbb C^d$, is
$$F=P(dP\wedge dP)P.$$
For any local $C^2$ orthonormal frame $V:U\to\mathbb C^{d\times r}$ with $V^*V=I_r$ and $P=VV^*$, its connection matrix $A=V^*dV$ is anti-Hermitian and its curvature matrix is $F_{\mathrm{fr}}=dA+A\wedge A=V^*FV$. If $V'=Vg$ for a $C^2$ map $g:U\to U(r)$, then $A'=g^{-1}Ag+g^{-1}dg$ and $F'_{\mathrm{fr}}=g^{-1}F_{\mathrm{fr}}g$. Along every $C^2$ path, Kato transport is unitary and intertwines the endpoint projectors.
lem-nrqmx-c2-projector-chern-integrality:
## Statement

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a compact boundaryless oriented smooth surface, let $d\geq1$, and let $P:\Sigma\to\operatorname{End}(\mathbb C^d)$ be a $C^2$ family of rank-one orthogonal projections. Let $E_P\to\Sigma$ be the complex line bundle with fibers $\operatorname{ran}P(x)$, let $\nabla=P\,d$, and let $F=P(dP\wedge dP)P$ be the curvature of this projected connection. Then
$$\frac{i}{2\pi}\int_\Sigma\operatorname{tr}F=\langle c_1(E_P),[\Sigma]\rangle\in\mathbb Z.$$
Here $c_1(E_P)$ is the first integral Chern class of the underlying topological complex line bundle, and $[\Sigma]$ is the fundamental class for the stated orientation.
thm-nrqmx-adiabatic-geometric-phase-boun:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\geq1$, let $H\in C^2([0,1],\operatorname{Herm}(\mathbb C^d))$ be a finite Hermitian family with energy unit joules, and let $\hbar>0$ have unit joule-seconds. A spectral cluster at $s$ is a subset $\sigma_P(s)$ of the finite spectrum of $H(s)$, and $P(s)$ is the orthogonal projection onto the sum of its eigenspaces. Coherently followed means that $s\mapsto P(s)$ is continuous in operator norm (equivalently, it agrees locally with the Riesz continuation of its initial cluster). Assume the distance from $\sigma_P(s)$ to the complementary spectrum is at least a uniform $g>0$ in joules. Let $T>0$ be a total duration in seconds, let $s=t/T$ be dimensionless, and let $U_T(0)=I$ solve
$$i\hbar\,\partial_sU_T(s)=T H(s)U_T(s).$$
Put $K(s)=[P'(s),P(s)]$. There is a $C^1$ Hermitian matrix $X(s)$ solving $[H(s),X(s)]=K(s)$. With
$$C=2\sup_{s\in[0,1]}\|X(s)\|+\int_0^1\bigl(\|X'(s)\|+\|K(s)\|\,\|X(s)\|\bigr)\,ds,$$
the leakage satisfies
$$\|(I-P(s))U_T(s)P(0)\|\leq\frac{\hbar C}{T}\qquad(0\leq s\leq1).$$
The supplier provides a $C^1$ Hermitian $X$ solving the displayed commutator equation. For that $X$, $C$ has unit joule-inverse, so $\hbar C/T$ is dimensionless. If the cluster has rank one, with $H(s)P(s)=E(s)P(s)$, define $U_A(0)=I$ by
$$i\,\partial_sU_A(s)=\left(\frac{T}{\hbar}H(s)+iK(s)\right)U_A(s).$$
For Kato transport $W'(s)=K(s)W(s)$, $W(0)=I$, the comparison evolution factors exactly on the initial eigenspace:
$$U_A(s)P(0)=\exp\!\left(-\frac{iT}{\hbar}\int_0^sE(u)\,du\right)W(s)P(0).$$
The leakage estimate is finite-dimensional and conditional on the stated uniform positive gap.
thm-nrqmx-rank-one-chern-holonomy:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $\Sigma$ be a compact boundaryless oriented smooth surface, and let $P:\Sigma\to\operatorname{End}(\mathbb C^d)$ be a $C^2$ rank-one orthogonal projection family. Let $E_P$ be its complex line bundle, $\nabla=P\,d$, and $F=P(dP\wedge dP)P$. Then
$$\frac{i}{2\pi}\int_\Sigma\operatorname{tr}F=\langle c_1(E_P),[\Sigma]\rangle\in\mathbb Z.$$
For any $C^2$ closed path $\gamma$ subdivided into local unit frames $u_j$, with $A_j=u_j^*du_j$ and transition $u_{j+1}=u_jg_j$ for $g_j$ valued in $U(1)$ at the crossing points, the holonomy is the scalar by which parallel transport acts on its one-dimensional initial fiber. This scalar is the product of the local factors $\exp(-\int_{\gamma_j}A_j)$ and the transition factors $g_j^{-1}$. Thus geometric holonomy includes the frame-transition scalars whenever one frame does not cover the path.

In addition, suppose $\Sigma=\Sigma_N\cup\Sigma_S$ is a decomposition into compact oriented subsurfaces with disjoint interiors and common finite boundary $\Gamma=\partial\Sigma_N=-\partial\Sigma_S$, a finite union of oriented smooth circles. If $E_P$ has supplied $C^2$ unit frames $u_N,u_S$ on these subsurfaces and $u_S=u_Ng$ on $\Gamma$ for a $C^2$ map $g:\Gamma\to U(1)$, then
$$\langle c_1(E_P),[\Sigma]\rangle=\operatorname{wind}(g):=\sum_{\Gamma_j\subset\Gamma}\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{\Gamma_j}g^{-1}dg\in\mathbb Z,$$
where each component $\Gamma_j$ has the orientation induced by $\partial\Sigma_N$.
lem-nrqmx-spin-half-solid-angle-period:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $S^2$ be the unit sphere with outward area form $\omega$, and set
$$\sigma_x=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad\sigma_y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad\sigma_z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad P_+(n)=\frac{I+n_x\sigma_x+n_y\sigma_y+n_z\sigma_z}{2}.$$
For any two $C^2$ maps $f_0,f_1:D^2\to S^2$ from an oriented disk, with the same boundary map and its induced boundary orientation, the two oriented solid-angle integrals differ by a multiple of $4\pi$:
$$\int_{D^2}f_0^*\omega-\int_{D^2}f_1^*\omega\in4\pi\mathbb Z.$$
